feedback.problem: If the path $C$ is a part of the graph $y={x}^{3}$ traversed from the point $P(1,1)$ to point $Q(2,8),$ then ${\int }_{C}\frac{1}{y}\,dx+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,dy=$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that our curve is given by the explicit Cartesian equation $y={x}^{3}.$ As a result, we obtain the following parametrization of the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t)=x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j=t\,i+{t}^{3}\,j,\,t\in [1,2]\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=i+3{t}^{2}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\frac{1}{y}\,dx+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,dy & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{y}\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(\frac{1}{y}\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{{t}^{3}}\cdot 1+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\cdot 3{t}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{{t}^{3}}+3\,\text{d}t \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{2{t}^{2}}+3t]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =[-\frac{1}{2({2}^{2})}+3(2)]-[-\frac{1}{2({1}^{2})}+3(1)] \\  & =-\frac{1}{8}+6+\frac{1}{2}-3 \\  & =\frac{27}{8}\end{aligned}
$$
